attestations.notes: Read items/thm-the-empty-set-exists-and-is-unique.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: nonempty first-order domain supplies a set; Separation with z≠z gives no members; Extensionality gives uniqueness. The empty and uniqueness boundaries are explicit at steps 3.1–4.1.

Read items/lem-the-intersection-of-a-nonempty-set-is-a-set.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: x≠∅ yields B∈x; Separation on B defines the intersection; B∈x makes the bounded and unbounded predicates equivalent; Extensionality removes dependence on B. The nonempty premise is used at step 1.1.

Read items/lem-the-power-set-of-a-set-is-a-set.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: Power Set provides a bounding set of all subsets, Separation fixes exact membership, and Extensionality gives uniqueness. The x=∅ case follows from the same predicate; no choice is used.

Read items/lem-unions-and-intersections-of-small-families.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: steps 1.1–1.5 expand union/intersection membership for ∅, singleton, and pair; singleton/pair indexing is nonempty where intersection is used, and Extensionality closes all equalities.

Read items/lem-ordered-pairs-lie-in-the-double-power-set.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: a∈A and b∈B place both in A∪B; the two components {a} and {a,b} are subsets, so the Kuratowski pair is a subset of P(A∪B). Empty ambient sets make the given premise vacuous.

Read items/lem-unordered-pair-equality.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: right-to-left is elementwise; left-to-right separates a=b from a≠b and rules out the crossed contradiction. Step 4.1 specializes b=a for singleton equality; both iff directions and coincident elements are covered.

Read items/thm-the-characterising-property-of-ordered-pairs.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: expand Kuratowski pairs and apply unordered-pair equality to the outer pair; both alternatives force a=c and b=d, including collapsed inner pairs. The reverse implication is immediate by substitution.

Read items/lem-the-domain-and-range-of-a-relation-are-sets.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: every component of a Kuratowski pair in R lies in ⋃⋃R; Separation on that bound defines domain and range. R=∅ works with the same bound and predicate.

Read items/lem-omega-smallest-inductive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: Infinity gives I0; Separation inside I0 defines members common to every inductive set; closure and leastness follow, and Extensionality proves uniqueness. Empty candidate family is excluded by I0.

Read items/thm-induction-principle.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: a subset containing 0 and successor-closed is inductive, so omega leastness yields equality; Separation on omega turns a property into the subset form, with the converse immediate.

Read items/lem-nat-transitive-irreflexive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: simultaneous induction proves transitivity and n∉n; successor transitivity splits x∈n or x=n, while either way σ(n)∈σ(n) would imply n∈n. The base n=∅ is explicit.

Read items/thm-recursion.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: intersect all closed subsets of N×A to get a minimal closed relation; induction gives totality, and removing an extra value at 0 or σ(n) contradicts minimality using P1/P2. A final induction proves uniqueness of the function. Requires a∈A, so no empty-A exceptional case.

Read items/thm-omega-is-peano-system.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction is inherited, successors contain n so are nonzero, and equality of successors with m≠n would yield m∈n and n∈m, contradicting transitivity and irreflexivity. Thus P1–P3 hold.

Read items/cor-nat-addition-well-defined.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: recursion on the Peano system with A=N, initial m and f=σ gives unique total s_m; definition m+n=s_m(n) satisfies both displayed clauses.
Read items/lem-nat-add-associative.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on c; base uses right-zero clause and successor step applies recursive addition twice around the inductive equality.
Read items/lem-nat-add-identity.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on n proves 0+n=n by the right-argument recursion; n+0=n is the defining clause.
Read items/lem-nat-add-successor-left.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on n, with n=0 from right-zero and successor step rewriting both sides through the defining right-argument recursion.
Read items/lem-nat-add-commutative.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on n uses 0 as two-sided identity and the separately proved left-successor law to match m+σ(n) with σ(n)+m.

Read items/lem-nat-add-cancellative.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on common right summand k; zero reduces to equality and successor reduces by injectivity of σ before applying the induction hypothesis.
Read items/lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: the subset {0 or successor} contains 0 and every σ(n), so induction exhausts N; the nonzero branch is then a successor.

Read items/lem-nat-trichotomy.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: cancellation and no-zero-successor exclude opposite strict inequalities; induction on n establishes comparability, splitting m<n, m=n and m>n, with nonzero difference written as a successor. Zero and immediate-successor cases are handled.

Read items/thm-nat-linear-order.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: right-zero gives reflexivity, associativity transitivity, trichotomy totality; antisymmetry cancels m from m+(k+j)=m, then nonzero-successor rules out a nonzero sum equalling 0.

Read items/lem-nat-discrete.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: nonzero additive witness j=σ(i) converts m<n to σ(m)≤n; the converse converts σ(m)≤n to a nonzero witness and excludes m=n by cancellation. The open interval (n,σ(n)) is empty.

Read items/lem-a-relation-is-included-in-the-product-of-its-domain-and-range.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: coordinate definitions give the first inclusion; both directions of the product criterion use ordered-pair coordinate uniqueness. Empty R makes all inclusions vacuous.

Read items/lem-inverse-relations-composites-and-restrictions-are-sets.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: inverse and composite relations are separated inside products of existing domain/range sets; restriction is separated inside R. Each formula uses existing set parameters; empty relations are covered.
Read items/lem-nat-successor-neq-self.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction starts with P1 at zero, and injectivity of σ makes any successor fixed point descend to a previous fixed point.

Read items/lem-nat-order-is-membership.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction makes N transitive; additive order plus discreteness yields m<σ(n) iff m≤n; two inductions identify strict order with membership. Steps 5.1–5.2 identify ≤ with inclusion using irreflexivity; zero and successor boundaries are explicit.

Read items/lem-pigeonhole.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: transposing codomain values normalizes a hypothetical injection σ(σ(n))→σ(n); restriction yields forbidden σ(n)→n, with n=0 handled. Restrictions/transpositions then derive size, infinity, and proper-subset consequences; no choice is needed beyond selecting one element of a nonempty finite difference.

Read items/thm-well-ordering-principle.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: assuming a nonempty S without a least element, the set of n with no S-member ≤n contains 0 and is successor-closed using discreteness/trichotomy; induction makes S empty, a contradiction.
Read items/cor-nat-multiplication-well-defined.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: recursion on the Peano system with initial 0 and endomap x↦x+m yields unique total p_m and the multiplication clauses.

Read items/lem-nat-order-add-compatible.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: associativity/commutativity transport an additive witness across a common summand, and cancellation recovers the witness; equality cancellation gives the strict variant.
Read items/lem-nat-mult-identity.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: n·1=n follows directly from recursion; simultaneous induction establishes 0·n=0 and 1·n=n, including n=0.

Read items/lem-nat-mult-distributive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on c proves a(b+c)=ab+ac; a separate induction on n proves σ(a)·n=a·n+n by rearranging sums with additive associativity/commutativity. Both zero bases appear.
Read items/lem-nat-mult-commutative.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on n compares right multiplication recursion to the previously derived successor-left law; zero case uses 0·m=0.
Read items/lem-nat-mult-associative.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: induction on c, with multiplication recursion and left distributivity converting the successor step to a(b·σ(c)).

Read items/lem-nat-no-zero-divisors.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: for nonzero m,n write both as successors; multiplication recursion writes mn as a successor, hence nonzero by Peano P1. Zero cases are excluded only in the contrapositive.

Read items/lem-nat-order-mult-compatible.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: a witness n=m+d gives nk=mk+dk, so monotonicity holds even at k=0; for strictness d,k≠0 and no-zero-divisors plus cancellation force dk≠0 and distinct products.

Read items/lem-int-add-well-defined.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: equivalence equations add and rearrange to establish representative independence of componentwise sum; swapping coordinates preserves the relation for negation.

Read items/lem-int-mul-well-defined.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: expand the natural-number equivalence for one factor, factor with c,d, and use symmetric multiplication to handle the other factor; chaining gives independence of both representatives.

Read items/thm-int-comm-ring.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: prior well-definedness permits representative calculations; steps 1.2–1.9 check additive group, multiplicative associativity/commutativity/unit, and distributivity, including the explicit inverse pair.

Read items/thm-int-ordered-ring.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: adding equivalence equations and cancellation proves order independent of representatives; natural order supplies totality, antisymmetry, transitivity, and translation invariance; positive gaps k,m yield positive product gap km.
Read items/lem-of-zero-mult.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: distributivity writes 0a=0a+0a, while additive identity writes 0a=0a+0; cancellation yields 0a=0.

Read items/lem-of-add-order.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: differences are invariant under common translation, and the sum of two positive differences is positive by cone closure; both strict inequality claims follow.
Read items/lem-of-mult-neg.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: distributivity and zero multiplication identify (-a)b and a(-b) as additive inverses of ab; a second inverse calculation gives (-a)(-b)=ab.

Read items/lem-of-sign-rules.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: positive-cone closure proves three sign products and forward order scaling; converse directions use trichotomy to exclude equality/opposite order after multiplication. The hypotheses c>0 and c<0 exclude zero.
Read items/lem-of-square-positive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: trichotomy for nonzero a gives a>0 or -a>0; cone closure and (-a)^2=a^2 prove positivity in both cases.
Read items/cor-of-one-positive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: field axiom 1≠0 permits application of nonzero-square positivity to 1^2=1.

Read items/lem-of-inverse-positive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: the inverse of a positive a cannot be negative because aa^-1=1>0; multiplying 0<a<b by the positive a^-1b^-1 reverses the reciprocal sizes, with b^-1 positive.

Read items/lem-of-inverse-unique.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: group identity and inverse uniqueness use associativity and the identity equations in additive F and multiplicative F\{0}; the latter is restricted to nonzero elements.

Read items/lem-int-cancellation.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: ordered-ring trichotomy and sign rules show products of nonzero integers cannot vanish; distributivity then applies this to (x-y)z=0 for cancellation.

Read items/lem-rat-ops-well-defined.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: cross-multiplication identities for equivalent representatives expand to equivalent sum/product pairs; negation preserves the relation. Nonzero denominator products follow from the integer domain lemma.

Read items/thm-rat-field.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: fixed representatives verify ring laws, with distributivity established by cross multiplication; a nonzero class has nonzero numerator and inverse [(b,a)], using integer no-zero-divisors for denominator validity.

Read items/thm-rat-ordered-field.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: positive denominators permit order-scaling/cancellation, proving representative independence, transitivity and translation invariance; positivity of numerator products gives positive rational products. The positive-denominator convention is used throughout.

Read items/lem-identity-unique.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: evaluate e*f as f by left identity and e by right identity; applying that equality yields uniqueness of a two-sided identity and of one-sided identities when one exists. Associativity is not used.

Read items/lem-inverse-unique.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: in a monoid, h=h*(g*h’)=(h*g)*h’=h’; hence left and right inverses coincide. The consequences for an invertible g follow by pairing any one-sided inverse with its existing two-sided inverse; associativity is essential.

Read items/lem-of-naturals-positive.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: positivity and strict increase follow from adding 1_F>0; separate inductions give the additive and multiplicative identities for positive natural indices, then injectivity follows from strict increase.

Read items/lem-nat-embeds-int.md §§Statement/Facts/Proof: class equality proves injectivity, representative formulas preserve + and ·, integer order reduces to natural order, and a≥b gives [(a,b)]=[(k,0)] for unique k.
